choice.clFeeControllerNote: 1.1.0, deployed 2026-09-06, REPLACING 0x36ab137ac1647c16646CA851c2715FBb60f4FD3C. Carries zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee (plan A0, tokenomics D30/D31): a sprout.fun graduate pays Choice NO protocol fee, so protocolFeesAccrued holds only Choice's own revenue by construction. launchPoolGuardHook is set to choice.launchPoolGuardHook; while it is unset every graduation reverts. Owner = timelock. ⚠️ It ships PARKED - treasuryBps 10000, burnSink = directTransferBurnSink - and it is NEVER pointed at the SPROUT buybackBurnSink. The controller it replaces WAS (treasuryBps 2000 -> the SPROUT sink), which was the SPROUT_TOKENOMICS 9.0 walk configuration and is exactly the link D30 forbids. So Choice's own protocol fee no longer feeds the SPROUT buyback on testnet either; sprout's revenue reaches its sink only through launchpad.treasury and PositionLocker.launchpadTreasury. The superseded controller is left in place, timelock-owned, holding nothing, with nothing pointing at it.
choice.infinitySettlerNote: 1.2.0, deployed 2026-09-06, superseding 1.1.0 0x8C4f5418Ff1fb1eA80fA0c5b1e1c4604a7bdfA2d (same code, wrong locker) and 1.0.0 0xC3ED6d3f97D85B243108446a17ed53d896331ac9. Plan A0: lpFee 10000 (the WHOLE 1.00% tier, not the 6722 that composited to 1% alongside a protocol fee) and settle() calls clFeeController.zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee, so a graduate never charges Choice's protocol fee for even one block. The trader pays the same 1%: 9,999 pips before, 10,000 after. Owner = timelock. 🔴 1.1.0 is DEAD - its immutable LOCKER is the 1.0.0 locker, whose register() takes FOUR arguments (pre-contracts-2cf25cc) and therefore has no selector for the five-argument one this repo compiles. Every graduation through it reverted with EMPTY returndata after passing every gate and canary; launch #18 is wedged in CurveFilled because it snapshotted 1.1.0. Script 05 now proves the locker's ABI before it wires anything - see _requireLockerSpeaksOurAbi.
choice.positionLockerNote: 1.1.0, deployed 2026-09-06, REPLACING 0x9b28F31B8AB8ED488B4E8bc7cb432ceaFe60E3Fe. Plan A3, forced early by A0: the PULL version - collect() credits and claim() pays, so one blocked recipient cannot freeze the other side's fees - and register() binds the position to its PoolKey. That fifth argument changes the SELECTOR, which is why the 1.0.0 locker cannot serve any settler built from main. Born owned by the timelock and already pointing at settler 1.2.0. ⚠️ The 1.0.0 locker stays live and holds the positions of launches 13-17; their creator and launchpad fees are still collectable there, through its own push-payment collect(). Nothing new registers into it.
choice.buybackBurnSinkNote: TEST deployment, 2026-09-06, REPLACING 0xe0248Ebc4C87669aDCf8edf926B81D41319bB4af - which carried the settle that could still revert (contracts #12). Same constructor arguments and the same guards as the one it replaces. ⛔ The OLD clFeeController 0x36ab137a was repointed here on 2026-09-06 and the 1.1.0 controller that replaced it is NOT - see clFeeControllerNote. Under D30 a ChoiceFeeController is never pointed at the SPROUT sink; this sink is fed by the pad, through launchpad.treasury and PositionLocker.launchpadTreasury. Burn token is the TEST SPROUT 0xD21C10dCb94cD049f9544cc35D2bE6A76fD8D835 (launch 15), quote wINJ. Owner = timelock. MIN_BURN_BPS 8000 (immutable), burnBps 8000. Guards are TEST values chosen to make one session's volume visible - minBuybackInterval 60s, maxImpactBps 500, minBuybackAmount 1e15. See SPROUT_TOKENOMICS.md 9.0 and 9.3; do NOT copy these guards to mainnet. The superseded sink is left in place, owned by the timelock and holding nothing; no controller points at it.

addressAliases.choice.treasury: the Safe: protocol revenue lands where the signers can move it without waiting out a timelock delay

launchpad.core: shroom_launchpad LaunchpadCore on 1439, deployed 2026-08-24. Not ours; the pad admin owns it and only the pad admin can setSeederFactory.
launchpad.treasury: the launchpad's FeeTreasury: PositionLocker sends the non-creator share of graduated LP fees here
launchpad.phase3Settler: the CW graduation path this one replaces, kept for reference

addressAliases.choice.infinitySettler: M4 graduation adapter. The launchpad core's seederFactory since 2026-09-05: LaunchpadCore.triggerGraduation transfers both legs here and calls settle, which initialises the CL pool at realPair/poolTokenAmount, mints one full-range position to positionLocker and calls onSettled - all in that one transaction.
addressAliases.choice.positionLocker: Permanent home for every graduated launch's seed position. collect(launchId) is permissionless and splits the LP fees creator / launchpad.treasury by the launch's own creatorFeeShareBps; nothing in it can move the liquidity or the NFT.
addressAliases.choice.launchPoolGuardHook: beforeInitialize ONLY (bitmap 1), so it is consulted once in a pool's life and can never tax, block or freeze a swap. It permissions graduation-pool creation to the settler (D15), which is why every graduation pool is keyed to it forever.
addressAliases.choice.choiceRouter: M5.4 cross-vault router: one end-to-end minimumReceive across TWO Infinity deployments. Only Choice's vault exists on 1439, so execute() reverts NotCrossVault here by design - single-deployment routes go straight to the universalRouter. A second vault is added with setVault from the timelock.
addressAliases.pools: The bin entry carries binStep where the CL ones carry tickSpacing. Both pack at offset 16 of `parameters`, so the words are identical for the same number and only `poolType` tells them apart here - as on chain, where only PoolKey.poolManager does.

firstGraduation.note: The first launch to graduate onto Choice v2, walked end to end on testnet 2026-09-05. Recorded because the poolId and tokenId are the only durable handles on it: Injective serves no receipt, so nothing else can be looked up from the transaction hash.
firstGraduation.quoteAssetNote: the launchpad's own testnet USDC (6dp), NOT external.usdc - the pad quotes its own
firstGraduation.graduationGasNote: measured, not estimated: block 139052885 held this transaction alone, so the block's gasUsed IS the transaction's

a0Graduation.note: Plan A0 / tokenomics D30+D31 proven on chain: the FIRST launch to graduate paying Choice no protocol fee. Recorded because Injective testnet serves no receipt by hash, so the poolId is the only durable handle. Read getSlot0(poolId) on infinity.clPoolManager: protocolFee 0, lpFee 10000. The wall was checked both ways in the same session - the wINJ/USDT pool below still reads protocolFee 671908 (164 per direction) and zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee reverts NotALaunchPool on it.
a0Graduation.quoteAssetNote: the pad's testnet SAI, 18dp - the launch token is the EVM-only issuance lane (denom erc20:0xb654...), so no Cosmos message was involved in creating it
a0Graduation.compositeSwapFeeNote: calculateSwapFee(0, 10000) = 10000, exactly the 1.00% tier. The pre-A0 split charged calculateSwapFee(3299, 6722) = 9,999 - one pip in a million less, so A0 is trader-neutral to within that pip.
a0Graduation.permissionlessRepairProven: zeroLaunchPoolProtocolFee on this key, called from 0x...dEaD, succeeds and changes nothing - the function is permissionless and idempotent
a0Graduation.currencyOrderNote: currency0 is the QUOTE here and currency1 the launch token, because 0x7E6f < 0xb654 - the settler sorts by address, so which leg is currency0 differs per launch. Derivable from the two addresses above; not repeated as its own field, because a value that appears under two keys is exactly what the address book's duplicate check exists to catch.
